title: Lord's Supper
definition: The Lord's Supper is an ordinance given by Christ in which believers remember His death, proclaim the Gospel, and share communion as His people.
summary: The Lord's Supper calls believers to remember Christ's sacrifice and proclaim His death until He comes.
christFocus: Jesus gave the Supper to point His people back to His body given and blood shed for the forgiveness of sins.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Lord's Supper is a sacred ordinance of remembrance, proclamation, and fellowship. In it, believers remember the body and blood of Christ given for sinners.

The Supper does not repeat Christ's sacrifice. His sacrifice is finished. Instead, the Supper points the Church back to the cross and forward to His return. It proclaims the Gospel visibly.

The Supper also calls believers to self-examination, unity, gratitude, and reverence. It is not a casual ritual but a Christ-centered act of worship among God's people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Believers can forget the cost of redemption and drift into routine religion. The Lord's Supper matters because it repeatedly brings the Church back to the cross and reminds believers that they live by Christ's sacrifice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the Lord's Supper with faith, gratitude, repentance, and love for the body of Christ. Let it renew your focus on the cross, strengthen your hope, and deepen unity with fellow believers.
